title: Design a Real-Time Ad Click Aggregator
candidate_brief: Design a service that collects advertising click events and makes campaign activity available to advertisers.
prompt: Design a real-time ad click aggregation and analytics pipeline. Ad clicks arrive at massive volume; advertisers need near-real-time dashboards of clicks, impressions and spend per campaign and time period, plus accurate totals for billing.
blurb: A streaming aggregation firehose where the dashboard can be approximate but billing must be exact — windowing, dedup, and the hot-campaign skew.

rubric.label: Requirements gathering
rubric.description: Separates functional (ingest clicks, aggregate per campaign/time window, real-time dashboard, accurate billing totals, query by dimensions) from non-functional (ingest scale, low query latency, accuracy for billing, late-data handling).

rubric.label: Clarifying questions
rubric.description: Asks about click volume, dashboard freshness SLA, accuracy requirement (approx dashboard vs exact billing), dimensions/cardinality, late/out-of-order events, retention.

rubric.label: Back-of-envelope estimations
rubric.description: Click events/s, bytes/s, aggregation cardinality (campaigns × windows × dims), storage for raw + rollups, query QPS.

rubric.label: Streaming pipeline architecture
rubric.description: Ingest → queue (Kafka) → stream processor (Flink/Spark) → aggregation store → query API; why a log-backed pipeline. Central senior signal.

rubric.label: Time windowing
rubric.description: Tumbling/sliding/session windows, event-time vs processing-time, watermarks, allowed lateness, handling out-of-order clicks. Central senior signal.

rubric.label: Deduplication & exactly-once
rubric.description: Dedup replayed/duplicate clicks (click_id), exactly-once processing (checkpointing, idempotent sink), why at-least-once ingest + dedup, billing accuracy. Central senior signal.

rubric.label: Hot partition / skew handling
rubric.description: A viral campaign overwhelms one partition/key; salting/sub-keys + two-stage aggregation, backpressure, adaptive partitioning.

rubric.label: API design
rubric.description: click ingest endpoint, aggregate query (campaign, time range, granularity, dims), event schema.

rubric.label: Data model
rubric.description: raw event log, pre-aggregated rollups by (campaign, window, dims), dedup store; OLAP store choice.

rubric.label: Accuracy, reconciliation & reprocessing
rubric.description: Fast approximate path vs accurate batch path (lambda/kappa), reprocessing from raw log for corrections and billing, reconciliation.

rubric.label: Scaling
rubric.description: Partitioning by campaign/key, scaling stream operators, OLAP store for high-cardinality queries, retention tiers.

rubric.label: Bottlenecks
rubric.description: Hot campaign key, dedup-state memory, late-data recompute, high-cardinality query cost, checkpoint overhead.

rubric.label: Observability & reliability
rubric.description: Pipeline lag/watermark delay, dropped/late events, dedup rate, count accuracy vs billing reconciliation, backpressure alarms.

functional_requirements: Ingest ad click (and impression) events at high volume
Aggregate counts/spend per campaign per time window (minute/hour/day)
Query aggregates by dimensions (campaign, ad, geo, device)
Handle late and out-of-order events, and duplicate clicks
nonfunctional_requirements: Very high ingest throughput (100Ks–millions of events/s)
Dashboard freshness within seconds to ~1 minute
Approximate is OK for the live dashboard; billing totals must be accurate/exact
Resilient to spikes and viral (hot) campaigns; no data loss for billing
clarifying_questions: Dashboard freshness SLA — seconds, or a minute is fine?
How exact must counts be — is the live dashboard allowed to be approximate while billing is exact?
Which dimensions/granularities do advertisers slice by, and what's the cardinality?
How late can events arrive, and how out-of-order?
Retention for raw events vs aggregates?
qualifying_questions: Is a lambda (fast approx + accurate batch) architecture acceptable, or must a single path be exact?
Do we need dedup across a long window (replays/retries), and what's the dedup key?
Multi-region ingest with a global rollup, or single region?

estimations.traffic: Say 500K clicks/s peak (impressions much higher). At ~200B/event → ~100MB/s ingest; buffered in a partitioned log.
estimations.storage: Raw events retained for reprocessing/billing: 500K/s × 200B × 86400 ≈ ~8.6TB/day raw (compressed less) → tiered to cheap storage. Aggregates are far smaller: campaigns × windows × dims.
estimations.cardinality: Rollup cardinality = campaigns × time buckets × dimension combos; per-minute × many campaigns × geo×device can explode — pick granularities/dims deliberately.
estimations.queries: Dashboard queries are moderate QPS but hit an OLAP store; pre-aggregation keeps them cheap; ad-hoc high-cardinality slices are the expensive case.

core_components: Click ingest service (edge, lightweight, writes to log)
Stream processor (Flink/Spark Streaming) — windowed aggregation + dedup
Raw event store (object storage, for reprocessing/billing)
data_model: click_event(click_id UNIQUE, campaign_id, ad_id, ts (event time), user/device, geo, cost) — raw, append-only
rollups(campaign_id, window_start, granularity, dim_key, click_count, spend) — pre-aggregated, sink target
dedup_state: seen click_ids within a bounded window (RocksDB/keyed state / TTL'd store)
raw log partitioned by campaign_id (or salted key for hot campaigns)
billing_totals(campaign_id, day, accurate_count, accurate_spend) — from batch reprocessing
api_design: POST /v1/clicks { click_id, campaign_id, ad_id, ts, ctx } → 202 (fire-and-forget to log)
reference.high_level_design: Lightweight edge ingest services accept clicks and append them (at-least-once) to a PARTITIONED LOG (Kafka), which absorbs spikes and durably retains raw events. A STREAM PROCESSOR (Flink/Spark) consumes the log and performs windowed aggregation: it groups by (campaign, dimension) and reduces counts/spend into TIME WINDOWS (tumbling per-minute/hour) using EVENT TIME with WATERMARKS to tolerate out-of-order arrival and a configured ALLOWED LATENESS to fold in stragglers. It DEDUPES on click_id against keyed state (bounded by a window/TTL) so replayed or retried clicks aren't double-counted. Results are written IDEMPOTENTLY (upsert by (campaign, window, dim)) into an OLAP aggregation store that serves fast dashboard queries. Because the live path favors freshness, it's treated as near-accurate; for BILLING, raw events are also archived to object storage and a periodic BATCH reprocessing job recomputes exact totals from the immutable log (lambda-style) and RECONCILES against the streaming numbers, correcting any drift from late data or dropped stream state. HOT CAMPAIGNS that would overwhelm a single partition/key are handled by SALTING the key (campaign_id + bucket) for a first-stage local aggregation, then a second stage combines the partials — two-stage aggregation avoids a single hot operator. Backpressure propagates from the processor through the log so ingest never drops billing data.

deep_dives.probe: A click happens at 10:00:59 but arrives at 10:01:30 due to mobile network delay. How would your design account for that click?
The same click gets sent twice after a client retry. How does your design avoid counting it twice?
A campaign goes viral and generates 40% of all clicks. How does your proposed design behave under that traffic?
The live dashboard showed 1.02 million clicks, but the final billing count differs. How would your design handle that discrepancy?
Many advertisers refresh the same dashboard just as its cached result expires. How would your design handle that load?
A campaign budget changes while clicks are still arriving. How does that update affect your pipeline?

scaling: Partition the event log by campaign_id (salted for hot keys)
Scale stream operators horizontally; parallelism per partition
OLAP store (Druid/ClickHouse/Pinot) for high-cardinality aggregate queries
Pre-aggregate to bound query cost; tier raw events to cheap storage
Two-stage aggregation to spread hot-key load
bottlenecks: Hot campaign key skewing one partition/operator
Dedup-state memory growth over the dedup window
Late-data recompute and window state size
High-cardinality ad-hoc queries on the OLAP store
tradeoffs: Fast approximate dashboard vs exact billing (lambda: two paths, more complexity) vs single exact path (kappa: simpler, higher latency)
Larger allowed lateness (more accurate, more state + delayed finalization) vs smaller (fast, drops stragglers)
Pre-aggregate fixed granularities (cheap queries, less flexible) vs raw-on-read (flexible, expensive)
Exactly-once (accurate, checkpoint/state cost) vs at-least-once + idempotent sink (simpler, needs dedup)
Fine dedup window (catches more dupes, more memory) vs coarse
alternative_solutions: Kappa architecture: one streaming path, reprocess by replaying the log (no separate batch layer)
Probabilistic sketches (HyperLogLog for unique users, count-min for heavy hitters) for cheap approximate dashboards
Pre-aggregation in the ingest tier (local counters flushed periodically) to cut event volume
Materialized views in the OLAP store for common rollups
observability: Dropped/too-late event count and dedup rate
Streaming-vs-batch count divergence (accuracy) + billing reconciliation breaks
Per-partition throughput to spot hot keys/skew
security: Click fraud/bot detection and filtering before billing
AuthN on query API; advertisers see only their campaigns
Rate limiting / validation on ingest; schema enforcement
PII minimization on user/device fields; encryption
Tamper-evident raw log for billing audit
reference.reference_answer: A strong answer builds a log-backed streaming pipeline: lightweight edge ingest appends clicks at-least-once to a partitioned log, a stream processor does event-time windowed aggregation with watermarks and allowed lateness to handle out-of-order clicks, dedupes on click_id in bounded keyed state, and writes idempotent upserts into an OLAP store for fast dashboards. It distinguishes the approximate live path from exact billing, keeping raw events for a batch/reprocessing path that recomputes exact totals and reconciles drift (lambda, or kappa via log replay). It handles hot viral campaigns with key salting + two-stage aggregation and backpressure so billing data is never dropped. The candidate protects hot dashboard rollups from cache stampede, enriches clicks against campaign/budget data via CDC into a compacted topic, and names the hot key, dedup-state memory, late-data recompute, and high-cardinality queries as the top bottlenecks with mitigations. Effective exactly-once = at-least-once ingest + checkpointing + idempotent sink + dedup, and freshness/accuracy is monitored via pipeline lag, watermark delay, and streaming-vs-batch reconciliation.

facts.reveal_when: The candidate asks about click volume, event rate, traffic or peak throughput. Give this fact alone unless other facts were requested.
The candidate asks about event size or payload size. Do not bundle this with a volume-only answer.

facts.value: Dashboard updates within 5–10 seconds are acceptable.
facts.reveal_when: The candidate asks about dashboard freshness, update latency or whether a 5–10-second target is acceptable.

facts.value: The live dashboard may be approximate; billing totals must be accurate.
facts.reveal_when: The candidate asks about accuracy requirements or approximation.

interviewer_notes: Let the candidate independently clarify scope and drive a coherent design before assessment questions. State the business problem without asking what they would clarify. Answer only each requested fact: volume, event size, freshness and accuracy have separate disclosure triggers. Do not add an assessment question to clarification answers. Observe diagram/code changes silently and wait while they draw, think or explain. After the candidate finishes or invites discussion, select one or two important unresolved areas from their actual design, such as late data, counting accuracy or skew. Ask one neutral question at a time without naming a technique they have not introduced, accept valid alternatives, and return the floor instead of cycling through every probe. Private assessment priorities include event-time correctness, bounded duplicate tracking, billing reconciliation and hot-campaign resilience. Record missing independent requirements gathering for feedback rather than coaching them to do it during the interview.
